vulnerabilities.description: The `format` GET parameter is directly concatenated into a shell command string without any sanitization, and then executed via PHP's `exec()` function. An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands by breaking out of the single-quoted date format string.
vulnerabilities.data_flow: User input ($_GET['format']) → TimeController::index() → new TimeModel($format) → $this->command = "date '" . $format . "' 2>&1" → exec($this->command)

vulnerabilities.description: The output of the shell command is directly embedded into the HTML response using `<?= $time ?>` without any HTML encoding or sanitization. When combined with the command injection vulnerability (VULN-001), an attacker can make the server execute a command that returns arbitrary JavaScript code, which will then be executed in the browser of any user viewing the page.
vulnerabilities.data_flow: Attacker-controlled command output → exec() → $time → TimeController::index() returns $time → Router::view('index', ['time' => $time]) → extract($data) → <?= $time ?> in HTML
